planted_anomaly_detections.note: the frozen 37/50/31 budget lives entirely in CUSTOMER_MASTER and INVOICE_LINE, which are wave 1 units; nothing in this unit's four tables carries a budgeted anomaly, and none was found

unverified_paths: Y/N-to-boolean, CSV-to-array and DD-MON-YY-string-to-date are graded by tier 4 operations, not by the canonicaliser: the harness has no rule for them and patching the harness was out of scope. Raised as profile feedback in .migration/canonicalization.json.
CODES-decoded fields (plans.tier, tenants.status, subscriptions.status) are graded by tier 4 operations, not tier 3, because the source holds integers and the target holds decoded strings.
subscription_history is empty at source (0 rows), so its field grading is structurally exercised but not value-exercised.

The repo self-check asks for an ow_tp / ow-tp- namespace prefix. The engagement intake fixes the target database as ow_billing_migration, so the prefix rule is deliberately not met; the allowlist in .migration/allowed_targets.json is the control instead.
Scale is the demo estate on an Atlas M0 cluster. Nothing here is a statement about production volumes.

The load reads Oracle in one read-only transaction, so it is snapshot-consistent; it is not serialised against a second concurrent loader, which the wave manifest's disjoint write targets prevent rather than the code.

tier3_keyed_diffs.mode: full_diff on every collection; no sampling

source_access: SELECT/WITH only, in a single read-only transaction; no DDL or DML against OW_BILLING
